title: Microsoft Intune: Windows quality update policies with per-type approval (GCC)
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the licensing, optional deployment, approval controls and pause behaviour, and the GCC roadmap facts match the supplied record. The creation path stops at the settings page rather than the deferral control, and the Worldwide roadmap comparison needs its own citation.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Intune policies to manage individual Windows quality updates, including non-security and out-of-band updates, with per-type automatic approval and rollout options.
claims.quote: Manage individual Windows quality updates including non-Security and out of band updates.  Choose which update types to automatically approve and the rollout options for those approvals.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The new control is admin-opt-in: devices without a quality update policy retain standard Windows Update behaviour.
claims.quote: Devices without a quality update policy continue to receive quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior, using update rings and Windows Update client policies to control deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications.

claims.claim: Monthly security updates have their own approval setting.
claims.quote: Monthly security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS cumulative quality updates and .NET Framework security updates.

claims.claim: Monthly non-security preview updates have their own approval setting.
claims.quote: Monthly non-security preview updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS preview updates and .NET Framework preview updates.

claims.claim: Out-of-band security updates have their own approval setting.
claims.quote: Out-of-band (OOB) security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS security OOB releases and .NET Framework security OOB releases.

claims.claim: Out-of-band non-security updates have their own approval setting.
claims.quote: Out-of-band non-security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS non-security OOB releases and .NET Framework non-security updates.

claims.claim: A single policy can set automatic or manual approval separately across update types.
claims.quote: A single policy can use both automatic and manual methods across different update types.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Monthly security updates default to automatic approval when creating a policy.
claims.quote: When you create a quality update policy, the default approval configuration of monthly security updates is automatic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The other update types default to manual approval.
claims.quote: The default approval configuration of other updates is manual.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Automatic approval deferrals range from 0 to 30 days.
claims.quote: The allowed range is 0 to 30 days for quality updates.

claims.claim: The same policy settings govern supported .NET Framework updates.
claims.quote: The quality update policy settings also govern supported .NET Framework updates in Windows Autopatch.

claims.claim: Manual approval holds deployment until explicit approval.
claims.quote: This configuration provides full control, deploying updates only with explicit manual approval.

claims.claim: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approval for security updates.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates.

claims.claim: Windows Autopatch recommends manual approval for optional updates.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates.

claims.claim: Pausing an approved update revokes its approval.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update, and no new devices receive it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A pause stops new devices receiving the selected release.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update, and no new devices receive it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Pausing does not roll back devices that already installed the update.
claims.quote: Devices that already installed the update aren't rolled back.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new pause settings.
claims.quote: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new update pause settings.

claims.claim: Reporting requires allowing Intune access to Windows diagnostic data from enrolled devices.
claims.quote: To enable reporting for this feature, ensure your organization allows Intune to access Windows diagnostic data collected from enrolled devices.

claims.claim: Devices need telemetry enabled with a minimum setting of Required.
claims.quote: Telemetry must be turned on, with a minimum setting of Required.

claims.claim: Automatically approved updates are offered to assigned devices after the configured deferral without another human approval.
claims.quote: Devices assigned to this policy receive an update after this many days since Microsoft releases the update.

claims.claim: Learn recommends keeping quality update deferrals under three days.
claims.quote: Keep quality update deferrals under three days.

claims.claim: An administrator can manually override the deferral and immediately approve an update.
claims.quote: Yes, you can manually override the deferral period and approve the update when needed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Cloud quality update policy approval settings and deferrals take priority over update ring deferrals on jointly targeted devices.
claims.quote: The quality update policy takes priority for approval settings and deferrals.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Other client settings, including update ring deadlines and grace periods, remain active.
claims.quote: Other update ring policy settings, such as deadlines and grace periods, remain active.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Changing the approval method requires creating a new policy rather than editing an existing one.
claims.quote: No, you can't change the approval method in an existing policy. If you need a different approval method, create a new policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Approved non-security updates are not delivered when the policy has hotpatch enabled.
claims.quote: If a policy has hotpatch updates enabled and non-security updates are approved, will the device receive the non-security updates? No, the devices won't receive non-security updates in this case.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to disable the policy hotpatch setting to receive non-security updates.
claims.quote: To receive non-security updates, disable the hotpatch update setting in the quality update policy.

claims.claim: The Intune page says Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported for this policy type and directs administrators to update rings.
claims.quote: Windows Enterprise LTSC (Long Term Service Channel) isn't supported. Use update ring policies instead.

claims.claim: The Autopatch overview and prerequisites separately describe quality update support for currently serviced Windows 10/11 LTSC devices.
claims.quote: The service only supports managing the Windows quality updates workload for devices currently serviced by the LTSC.

claims.claim: Windows 10 ESU devices receive .NET Framework updates through Windows Update client-side settings.
claims.quote: Windows 10 devices enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU) continue to receive .NET Framework updates from Windows Update based on client-side settings.

claims.claim: Quality update policy approvals apply only to OS quality updates on Windows 10 ESU devices.
claims.quote: On those devices, quality update policy approvals apply only to Windows OS quality updates.

claims.claim: The policy type supports Windows Pro, Pro Education, Enterprise and Education editions.
claims.quote: This feature supports the following Windows editions: - Pro - Pro Education - Enterprise - Education

claims.claim: The policy type requires Intune-managed devices.
claims.quote: This policy type supports devices that are: - Managed by Intune

claims.claim: Supported devices are Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra joined - Microsoft Entra hybrid joined

claims.claim: The Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service, wlidsvc, must be enabled and running.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service (`wlidsvc`) must be enabled and running.

claims.claim: Managed devices targeted by a quality update policy are automatically enrolled in Windows Autopatch, subject to the stated Insider exception.
claims.quote: Managed devices that are targeted to a quality update policy are automatically enrolled with the Windows Autopatch.

claims.claim: Windows Insider builds are not enrolled for quality updates and the approval settings do not apply to them.
claims.quote: If you add devices running Windows Insider builds to the approval policy, these devices won't be enrolled in Windows Autopatch for quality updates. Therefore, approval settings from the quality update policy don't apply.

claims.claim: A device removed from all quality update policies remains enrolled for 24 hours before automatic unenrolment.
claims.quote: When a device is no longer assigned to any quality update policies, the device remains enrolled in Windows Autopatch for 24 hours. ... After 24 hours, the device is automatically unenrolled from Windows Autopatch for quality updates.

claims.claim: Endpoint Security Manager, Read Only Operator and Help Desk Operator can view the reports.
claims.quote: To view the reports for this feature, use an account with at least one of the following roles: - Endpoint Security Manager - Read Only Operator - Help Desk Operator

claims.claim: A custom role with Managed devices/View Reports can view the reports.
claims.quote: Custom role with the Managed devices/View Reports permission.

claims.claim: The creation route in Microsoft Intune admin center is Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Create > Windows quality update policy > Settings.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates. ... Select Create. ... Select Windows quality update policy. ... Under Settings, choose your approval method configuration
claims.fix: For the automatic deferral control, extend the path to 'Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Create > Windows quality update policy > Settings > Make updates available after'. Retain the note explaining that approval methods are chosen under Settings; the intervening Basics name entry and Next do not need to be path steps.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies creates a policy with its approval settings.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies

claims.claim: The request body approvalSettings collection carries policy approval settings.
claims.quote: approvalSettings | windowsQualityUpdateApprovalSetting collection | The list of approval settings for this policy.

claims.claim: approvalSettings elements use approvalMethodType and deferredDeploymentInDay to specify approval and automatic deferral.
claims.quote: "approvalSettings": [ { ... "approvalMethodType": "automatic", "deferredDeploymentInDay": 7 } ]

claims.claim: The request body hotpatchEnabled property sets hotpatch.
claims.quote: hotpatchEnabled | Boolean | Indicates if hotpatch is enabled for the tenants.

claims.claim: The approval route is Microsoft Intune admin center > Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Manage updates > release > Approved policies > policy > Approve.
claims.quote: Select Manage updates. ... Select a Release name ... Select the X of Y under Approved policies to see which policies are approved. ... Select the desired policies and select Approve.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction performs the release action for a policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction

claims.claim: bulkAction takes action and an ids list in its request body.
claims.quote: | action | windowsQualityUpdatePolicyActionType | | | ids | String collection | |

claims.claim: action=approve approves a quality update.
claims.quote: | approve | 0 | Enum value to represent the approval actions for quality update |

claims.claim: action=suspend pauses a quality update.
claims.quote: | suspend | 1 | Enum value to represent the pause actions for quality update |

claims.claim: Pausing follows the same release and Approved policies route, ending at Pause instead of Approve.
claims.quote: Select Manage updates. ... select a Release name ... Select the X of Y under Approved policies ... Select the desired policies and select Pause.

claims.claim: Approved policies shows policies awaiting manual approval as Needs review.
claims.quote: The Approved policies column displays the number of policies that are approved and those that require manual approval. ... Policies that aren't approved are marked as Needs review for that release.

claims.claim: Release details show the included KBs for review before manual approval.
claims.quote: Select a Release name to see details, such as severity and included KBs. Use this information to review the payload before manual approval.

claims.claim: Policies target device groups and release approvals operate for those policies.
claims.quote: assignments | windowsQualityUpdatePolicyAssignment collection | List of the groups this profile is assgined to.

claims.where: controls notes; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documented Intune operations use Graph beta and Microsoft warns they are subject to more frequent change.
claims.quote: Microsoft supports Intune /beta APIs, but they are subject to more frequent change. Microsoft recommends using version v1.0 when possible.

claims.claim: A version 1.0 reference for these quality update policy operations has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: windowsQualityUpdatePolicy Microsoft Graph v1.0 quality update policy. Results document beta create, get, list, update and resource references; opened beta resource, create, bulkAction and approval-setting references. No v1.0 reference found.

claims.claim: Learn lists Public cloud and Government Community Cloud (GCC) as supported for quality update policies.
claims.quote: This feature is supported in the following cloud environments: - Public cloud - Government Community Cloud (GCC)

claims.claim: When a cloud quality update policy and legacy hotpatch-only quality update policy both apply, monthly security updates await manual or automatic approval.
claims.quote: Device assigned to cloud-based quality update policy and legacy quality update policy (with only the hotpatch update setting). The cloud-based quality update policy takes priority. That is, monthly security updates aren't offered to the device until you either manually or automatically approve them.
